3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The quantitative-genetic ceiling is H² = V_G/V_P =0.5, V_G = V_A+V_D+V_I. For any genotype-only predictor in population R²_pop ≤ V_G/V_P = H² =0.5, and for a linear additive predictor R² ≤ h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H². Hence A, R²_PGS cannot exceed 50% in population, is unconditional.

With N→∞ the marginal GWAS betas converge to true additive effects and a linearly summed PGS converges to h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H². The limit is 0.50 iff V_A = V_G i.e. V_D = V_I =0. H²=0.5, HWE and K-selection do not logically force V_D+V_I>0. So:

* B, R²→0.50 with arbitrarily large GWAS, is the purely additive special case h²=H². Not logically necessary; guaranteed limit is h² ≤0.5.
* C, linear sum will not approach 0.50 due to dominance/epistasis/non-linear effects, is the usual h² < H² statement. It is true conditional on V_D+V_I>0, which is the biological regularity for complex polygenic traits, but a degenerate purely additive architecture with V_D=V_I=0 and h²=H²=0.5 is formally compatible with the premises. Strictly logical necessity fails, practically taken as true.
* D, existence of epigenetic effects forces narrow-sense heritability <0.5, is not entailed. h² ≤ H² =0.5 always, equality attainable with V_A=V_G=0.5V_P while epigenetic variance sits in the 1-H² =0.5 non-genetic fraction of V_P. Epigenetic variation is standardly part of V_P−V_G.

Strict logical entailment from H²=0.5 alone therefore gives only A. That is the “only A” different combination covered by G. The conventional textbook idealisation V_D+V_I>0 for a complex K-selected trait makes h² < H² the practical expectation, giving the taught pairing A true, B false, C true in practice, D false, i.e. option E Only A and C. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 stress the strict necessity gap and favour G / essentially only A, while colleagues 10 and 7 argue the intended problem reading assumes the usual non-additive regularity and favour E. The core unresolved tension is strict formal necessity vs the empirical assumption that a realistic polygenic K-selected trait has non-zero dominance/epistatic variance, which would make C effectively true in practice.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population bound is unanimous. With H² = V_G/V_P =0.5 any genotype-based predictor satisfies R²(pop) ≤ V_G/V_P =0.5, and R²_PGS ≤ h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H². So A is necessarily true for a genotype based polygenic score.

The infinite-sample limit of the usual linear sum of marginal GWAS effects is the additive genetic variance:

R²∞ → h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H² =0.5, with equality iff V_G = V_A ⇔ V_D = V_I =0.

Hence

* B: R²∞ →0.50 requires h² = H² =0.5. H²=0.5 + HWE + K-selection do not logically force V_D+V_I>0 nor V_A<V_G. A purely additive architecture with V_G=V_A=0.5V_P, V_D=V_I=0 is formally compatible. So B is not logically necessary; it holds only in the degenerate purely additive case.

* C: the linear additive PGS cannot recover V_D and V_I, so its limit is h² < H² whenever V_D+V_I>0. That is the usual quantitative-genetics expectation for a complex K-selected trait and the textbook reason why a linearly summed score will not approach the broad-sense bound. Strictly, C is true conditional on non-zero non-additive variance; the premises alone allow V_D=V_I=0, in which case a linear PGS would attain R²→0.5. So C is not a logical necessity, it is the generic biological regularity.

* D: h² ≤ H² =0.5 always with equality attainable when V_G is purely additive. Under the standard DNA-sequence definition epigenetic variance is part of V_P – V_G, i.e. the 1-H² environmental fraction. With H² fixed at 0.5 we can still have V_A=V_G=0.5V_P while epigenetic variance sits in the remaining 0.5V_P non-genetic fraction. Existence of epigenetic effects does not by itself force h²<0.5.

Hence on strict logical entailment the only forced statement is A. That is the “only A’’ case, option G, with B,C,D not necessarily true.

The deliberation is split on interpretation. Colleagues 1,2,5,6,8,9 stress strict necessity → only A → G, noting the conventional textbook idealisation V_D+V_I>0 makes the usual taught pairing A true, B false, C true in practice, D false, i.e. option E. Colleagues 3,4,10,7 argue for the conventional biological reading and give E as the intended answer, taking h² < H² as given for a typical polygenic trait. Colleague 7’s earlier F is inconsistent with the bound.

Unresolved: whether the question asks for strict logical necessity from H²=0.5 alone, which gives A only → G, or for the usual biological expectation that a complex trait has non-zero dominance/epistatic variance, which gives the textbook A∧C → E. Current working belief remains: strictly A only, conventionally A and C.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population bound is settled. For any genotype-based predictor R²_pop ≤ V_G/V_P = H² =0.5, so A is an unconditional ceiling. For a linear additive PGS the infinite-sample limit is h² = V_A/V_P ≤ V_G/V_P = H², with equality iff V_G = V_A i.e. V_D = V_I =0.

Strict logical necessity from H²=0.5, HWE and K-selection alone:
* B R²∞→0.50 is h²=H². Not forced; h²=0.50 is compatible with H²=0.50 in a purely additive architecture.
* C “will not approach 0.50 due to dominance/epistasis/non-linear effects” is the usual h² < H² statement. It holds if V_D+V_I>0, but V_D=V_I=0 is formally compatible with the premises, so non-attainment is not logically necessary, only the generic biological expectation.
* D epigenetic existence forces h²<0.5. Not entailed. Under the DNA-sequence definition epigenetic variance sits in V_P-V_G = 0.5 V_P. With H² fixed we can still have V_A = V_G =0.5 V_P and h²=0.5.

Hence on strict entailment the only forced statement is A. That is the “only A” combination, option G. 

The conventional textbook reading adds the empirical regularity V_D+V_I>0 for a complex K-selected trait, i.e. h²<H² in practice. Under that extra biological assumption the taught pairing is A true, B false, C true in practice, D false, i.e. option E A∧C. Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly separate strict necessity of A from the conventional A∧C; colleagues 3,10,7 present E as the intended de-facto answer. Colleague 7’s F is inconsistent with the definitions.

Unresolved for me is whether the question asks for strict logical necessity or for the usual quantitative-genetics expectation. Current best strict reading remains only A → G. If the problem intends the usual empirical idealisation VD+VI>0, the intended answer is E.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The premises are H² = V_G/V_P = 0.5 in an ideal HWE K-selected population. V_G = V_A + V_D + V_I, h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H².

For any genotype-only predictor R²_pop ≤ V_G/V_P = H² =0.5. In particular for a polygenic score R²_PGS ≤ h² ≤ H² =0.5. Hence A is an unconditional population bound and is the only statement that follows from H²=0.5 alone.

With N→∞ and complete coverage the ordinary linear sum of marginal GWAS effects converges to the best linear additive predictor: R²_∞ → h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H². Equality R²_∞ =0.50 iff V_A = V_G i.e. V_D = V_I =0. The premises H²=0.5, HWE, K-selection do not force V_D+V_I>0 nor force V_A<V_G.

Therefore:
* B, R²→0.50 with arbitrarily large GWAS, is equivalent to h²=H²=0.5. It is not logically necessary; it holds only in the degenerate purely additive case V_G=V_A.
* C, linear sum will not approach 50% due to dominance/epistasis/non-linear effects, is the usual quantitative-genetic expectation h² < H² when V_D+V_I>0. It is true as a biological regularity for essentially all complex traits and is the textbook h² ≤ H² limitation, but it is not logically necessary from H²=0.5 alone because a purely additive architecture V_D=V_I=0, h²=H²=0.5 is formally compatible.
* D, existence of any epigenetic effects would limit narrow-sense heritability to <0.5, is not entailed. On the DNA-sequence definition H²=V_G/V_P, epigenetic variance is part of the 1-H² non-genetic fraction of V_P. With H² fixed at 0.5 we can still have V_A=V_G=0.5 V_P and accommodate V_epi>0 in the remaining 0.5 V_P environmental component. h² ≤ H² always, equality possible.

Consensus in the round: A is unavoidable. B is false in general. D is false. C is the conventional teaching point but its necessity depends on the extra empirical assumption V_D+V_I>0 for a complex trait.

Strict logical necessity: only A is guaranteed → the “different combination’’ case, essentially only A true, i.e. option G.

The textbook/practical reading that imposes the usual biological regularity V_D+V_I>0 gives A true, B false, C true in practice, D false, the A∧C pairing collected in option E. Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 stress the strict necessity distinction and favour G, colleagues 3,7,10 favour E as the intended answer. Unresolved is whether the question demands strict logical entailment from the stated premises alone or the conventional h²<H² idealisation for a polygenic K-selected trait.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The quantitative-genetic bounds are now settled in the discussion.

H² = V_G/V_P =0.5, V_G = V_A+V_D+V_I, h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H². Any genotype-only predictor has population R² ≤ V_G/V_P. Hence A “R²(PGS) cannot explain >50% of variance” is unconditional; it is the only bound that follows from H²=0.5 alone.

With N→∞ marginal GWAS betas converge to true additive effects and a linear sum converges to h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H². The limit is 0.5 iff V_A = V_G i.e. V_D=V_I=0. The premises H²=0.5, HWE, K-selection do not logically force V_D+V_I>0.

B “limit →50%” therefore is not logically forced; it is the purely additive special case h²=H². B is false in general.

C “linear sum will not approach 50% due to dominance/epistasis/non-linear effects” is the textbook h² < H² statement. A linear additive PGS can only recover V_A, so R²∞ = h² < H² whenever V_D+V_I>0. Strictly, V_D=V_I=0 with H²=h²=0.5 is formally compatible with the stated premises, so non-attainment is not a logical necessity, only the generic biological expectation for a complex polygenic trait. The discussion is split on this necessity point.

D “existence of any epigenetic effects would limit narrow-sense heritability to <0.5”. Under the standard DNA-sequence definition epigenetic variance is part of V_P – V_G, i.e. the 1-H² environmental fraction. With H² fixed at 0.5, h² ≤0.5 always and h²=0.5 is attainable with V_A=V_G=0.5V_P and epigenetic variance absorbed in the remaining 0.5V_P. Existence of epigenetics does not entail h²<0.5. D is not entailed.

Current public positions: a large majority invokes the conventional biological regularity V_D+V_I>0 for a K-selected complex trait and therefore treats C as practically necessary, giving A true, B false, C true in practice, D false → option E “Only A and C are correct”. Several colleagues, including myself in the previous round, stress the strict logical reading: without the extra V_D+V_I>0 assumption the only guaranteed statement is A, i.e. a different combination, essentially only-A, option G. The erroneous F position has been noted and rejected.

In the population sense the ceiling is the usual genotype ceiling

R²(G) ≤ VG/VP = H²

and for any genotype based predictor, in particular for an additive
polygenic score,

R²PGS ≤ h² = VA/VP ≤ VG/VP = H² =0.50,

so that the population upper bound

A. R²PGS ≤0.50

is unconditional.  That is the only bound that follows from H²=0.5 alone.

With N→∞ the marginal GWAS betas converge to the true additive
effects and the conventional linear sum converges to the best linear
additive predictor

R²∞(linear PGS) → h² = VA/VP.

Hence

R²∞ = h² ≤ VG/VP = H² =0.50

with equality iff VG = VA i.e. VD = VI =0.  A linear sum of marginal
effects can recover at most VA.  It cannot recover VD and VI and it
cannot recover any truly non-linear contribution to the phenotype.  For a
genuinely polygenic trait in a K-selected species the conventional
quantitative-genetic idealisation is VD+VI>0, i.e. h²<H², so that the
additive limit of the ordinary linear PGS is strictly below the broad
sense ceiling.  In that conventional idealisation

effects will not approach the broad-sense 0.50 because the score can only
recover VA.  Under the usual h²<H² regularity for a complex trait this is
the textbook additive vs broad-sense gap, i.e. R²∞=h²< H²=0.50.

attainable for VA=VG=0.5VP.  On the standard DNA-sequence definition of
VG epigenetic variation is part of VP–VG, i.e. of the 1–H² non-genetic
fraction.  With H² fixed at 0.5 we can have VA=VG=0.5VP and accommodate
Vepi>0 in the remaining 0.5VP environmental component.  The mere
existence of an epigenetic component therefore does not force h²<0.5,

* D is not entailed.

Hence on the usual quantitative-genetic empirical idealisation
VD+VI>0 for a complex K-selected polygenic trait the taught result is
A true, B false, C true in practice and D false, i.e. the A∧C pairing

public_text.7: {The strict logical reading correctly isolates A as the sole unconditional entailment from H²=0.5 alone, with B, C and D each requiring an extra biological premise (V_D + V_I > 0) that the problem statement does not explicitly supply. At the same time the problem specifies a “theoretically ideal population of a K-selected species” and “typical GWAS data,” both of which conventionally invoke the standard quantitative-genetic model in which non-additive variance is present for any polygenic trait. Under that modelling convention the linear PGS limit is necessarily h² < H², so C becomes true in practice while B and D remain false; the resulting A-and-C pairing is exactly option E. public_text.10: Colleague 7's framing aligns closely with the problem's emphasis on a "theoretically ideal population" of a K-selected species under HWE and "typical GWAS data" for a polygenic phenotype. While the purely additive edge case (VD = VI = 0) is formally admissible under H² = 0.5 alone, that degenerate scenario is biologically implausible for any realistic complex trait and is not what the question intends when it specifies typical GWAS construction. public_text.10: Colleague 7's emphasis on the problem's specific qualifiers—"theoretically ideal population of a K-selected species" plus "typical GWAS data"—is the right lens. Those constraints invoke the standard quantitative-genetic model in which non-additive components (dominance, epistasis) are present by default for any genuinely polygenic trait, so the infinite-sample linear PGS is bounded by narrow-sense heritability and cannot reach the broad-sense ceiling of 0.5. This makes both A (the unconditional genotype-based ceiling) and C (the linear marginal-effects construction necessarily misses V_D + V_I) logically entailed under the stated premises, while B is false and D does not follow from sequence-defined V_G. The resulting pairing is exactly E. The purely additive edge case that would allow B remains formally admissible in a vacuum but is excluded once the problem's conventional modelling assumptions are respected; therefore the group should converge on E rather than the stricter "only A therefore G" reading.

With H² = V_G/V_P = 0.5, for any DNA-only predictor R²_pop ≤ V_G/V_P = 0.5 and for a linear additive predictor R²_PGS ≤ h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H² = 0.5. Hence A is unconditionally true. That is the only statement that follows from H² = 0.5, HWE and K-selection alone.

V_G = V_A + V_D + V_I. With N→∞ the ordinary marginal GWAS linear sum converges to the best linear additive predictor R²_∞ → h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H², equality iff V_G = V_A ⇔ V_D = V_I = 0. The purely additive degenerate architecture V_A = V_G = 0.5 V_P, V_D = V_I = 0, h² = H² = 0.5 is formally compatible with all stated premises.

* B: R²_∞ → 0.50 is h² = H² = 0.5. Attainable in the purely additive case but not logically forced.
* C: a linear additive PGS can recover at most V_A, so R²_∞ = h² < H² whenever V_D+V_I > 0. This is the textbook h² ≤ H² limitation and the generic biological expectation for a complex K-selected trait, but non-attainment of 0.50 is not a logical necessity on H² = 0.5 alone; V_D = V_I = 0 would let a linear PGS reach 0.50.
* D: h² ≤ H² = 0.5 always, equality attainable with V_A = V_G. On the DNA-sequence definition epigenetic variance sits in V_P - V_G, i.e. the 1-H² fraction. With H² fixed at 0.5 we can still have V_A = V_G = 0.5 V_P while V_epi > 0 is absorbed in the remaining 0.5 V_P non-genetic variance. Existence of epigenetic effects does not by itself force h² < 0.5.

Strict logical entailment from the stated premises alone therefore yields only the ceiling A. B, C and D are not necessarily true. That is the “only A’’ different-combination case, option G.

Group split remains: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 maintain the strict necessity reading → only A → G, noting the conventional pedagogical reading is A true, B false, C true in practice, D false, i.e. A∧C → E. Colleagues 10 and 7 argue the problem’s qualifiers “theoretically ideal K-selected species” and “typical GWAS data” import the usual quantitative-genetic regularity V_D+V_I > 0, making C effectively necessary in context and the intended answer E. Unresolved tension is whether “necessarily true’’ means strict logical necessity from H² = 0.5 alone, which gives G, or conventional biological expectation that a realistic polygenic K-selected trait has non-zero dominance/epistatic variance, which gives E.

Current working belief remains strict: only A is forced; conventionally A and C are taught.

public_text.7: Colleague 7 and 10 make the key point that the problem's qualifiers—"theoretically ideal population of a K-selected species under HWE" plus "typical GWAS data"—are not neutral; they invoke the standard quantitative-genetic model in which non-additive variance (dominance and epistasis) is the expected default for any genuinely polygenic trait. Under that modeling convention, the infinite-sample linear PGS is bounded by narrow-sense heritability, so both the unconditional genotype ceiling (A) and the additive-only limitation (C) are entailed together. B is thereby ruled out and D does not follow from the sequence definition of V_G. This makes E the answer that best respects the problem's framing. The purely additive edge case remains formally admissible in a vacuum, but it is excluded once the conventional modelling assumptions implied by the wording are respected; the group should therefore converge on E.

Under that modelling convention the broad-sense ceiling H² = 0.5 is fixed while the additive fraction h² is strictly smaller, so the ordinary linear marginal-GWAS score is bounded by h² < 0.5 even as N → ∞. Consequently both A (the unconditional genotype ceiling) and C (the linear construction necessarily misses V_D + V_I) follow directly from the premises as written. B is thereby excluded and D remains false on the usual sequence-based definition of V_G. The resulting pairing is exactly E. The purely additive edge case that would allow B is formally admissible only if one strips away the problem’s modelling conventions; once those conventions are respected, E is the logically entailed and pedagogically intended answer.

The quantitative-genetic bounds are settled and stable across rounds.

* H² = V_G/V_P = 0.5, V_G = V_A + V_D + V_I, h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H².
* For any genotype-only predictor R²_pop ≤ V_G/V_P = H². Hence A “R²(PGS) ≤ 50%’’ is unconditional.
* With N → ∞ the ordinary marginal GWAS linear sum converges to the best linear additive predictor: R²∞ → h² = V_A/V_P ≤ H², equality iff V_G = V_A ⇔ V_D = V_I = 0.

Hence A is necessarily true.

B “R²∞ → 0.50’’ is h² = H². Formally compatible with H²=0.5, HWE and K-selection, so not logically forced.

C “linear sum will not approach 50% due to dominance/epistasis/non-linear effects’’ is the h² < H² statement. A linear additive score can only recover V_A, so R²∞ = h² < H² whenever V_D+V_I>0. Strictly V_D=V_I=0 is not ruled out by the stated premises alone, so non-attainment of 50% is biologically generic/empirical, not a strict logical necessity on premises as written. Most colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 now state C is not necessarily true without the extra premise, while 10 and 7 argue the qualifiers “theoretically ideal K-selected species under HWE” + “typical GWAS” implicitly import the conventional V_D+V_I>0 regularity.

D is not entailed. On the DNA-sequence definition h² ≤ H² always, with equality attainable for V_A = V_G. Epigenetic variance is part of V_P – V_G, i.e. the 1-H² =0.5 non-genetic fraction. With H² fixed at 0.5 we can have V_A = V_G =0.5 V_P while V_epi>0 is absorbed in the environmental fraction. Existence of epigenetics does not force h²<0.5.

Strict logical reading: the only unavoidable population fact from H²=0.5 alone is the genotype ceiling A. B, C and D each need the extra premise V_D+V_I>0. That is the “only A” case, option G.
Conventional textbook/empirical reading: “theoretically ideal K-selected polygenic phenotype with typical GWAS data” is taken to import V_D+V_I>0, h² < H². Under that contextualisation A is true, B is false, C is true in practice, D is false → the A∧C pairing, option E.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 articulate the strict core A only and note E only under the extra biological regularity. Colleagues 10 and 7 argue the problem’s qualifiers make the V_D+V_I>0 regularity intended, so E is the more precise/practically correct choice; the “only-A therefore G” reading is technically defensible in a vacuum but discards the wording.

Unresolved tension remains between strict necessity from premises as written → only A → G, versus the usual pedagogical idealisation → A∧C → E. Core facts A, h² ≤ H², R²∞ → h², D not entailed are now settled. Decision hinges on whether V_D+V_I>0 is considered implicit in “K-selected polygenic phenotype with typical GWAS”. Strict entailment favours G; conventional reading favours E.
